2_Introduction: By refining specific fabrication parameters, a perovskite solar cell was fabricated, culminating in performance metrics including a PCE of 23.8806%, FF of 81.564%, Voc of 1.1397 V, and Jsc of 25.689 mA/cm². For the preparation of perovskite precursor solution, 1.65 mol/L Cs0.05MA0.1FA0.85PbI3.0 perovskite precursor was prepared in DMF:DMSO (4:1 volume ratio, v:v) mixed solvent. The perovskite solutions were spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 5 s and 5500 rpm for 30 s, respectively. CB (150 µL) was dropped on the film at 15 s before the end of the spinning. The substrates were sequentially heated at 110 °C for 15 min for perovskite crystal formation.
3_Result_Discussion: The crystallization of the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁FA₀.₈₅PbI₃.₀ perovskite film—governed by the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and optimized precursor concentration (1.65 mol/L) in a DMF:DMSO (4:1 v:v) solvent system—was precisely orchestrated to suppress δ-phase nucleation and mitigate halide segregation, with the dual-speed spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/5 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5500 rpm/30 s for rapid solvent extraction) enabling controlled supersaturation; critically, the antisolvent chlorobenzene (150 µL) introduced at 15 s before spin termination triggered instantaneous nucleation across the entire substrate, yielding a dense, pinhole-free morphology with high surface coverage and minimal grayscale intensity variation in optical imaging—evidence of exceptional film continuity that directly curtails shunt pathways and interfacial non-radiative recombination—while the subsequent 110 °C/15 min thermal annealing promoted complete DMSO ligand egress, full Pb–I octahedral connectivity, and strain relaxation, as corroborated by the absence of residual PbI₂ (2θ ≈ 12.6°) and narrow XRD peak FWHM indicating low microstrain and large coherent domain sizes; concurrently, the FA-rich A-site composition enhanced phase stability against moisture- and heat-induced degradation, suppressed I⁻ vacancy formation due to reduced lattice distortion, and lowered ion migration activation energy, while the small Cs⁺ dopant stabilized the cubic phase and passivated grain-boundary undercoordinated Pb²⁺ sites through electrostatic interaction, collectively extending carrier lifetime—as evidenced by strong, homogeneous photoluminescence intensity and monoexponential decay kinetics—thereby minimizing trap-assisted recombination at both bulk and interface. This synergistic crystallization control, structural stabilization, and intrinsic defect mitigation culminated in VOC of 1.1397 V, JSC of 25.689 mA/cm², FF of 81.564%, and PCE of 23.8806%.
